instruction: You are a strategic corporate innovation advisor. Analyse the company profile and survey responses, then respond ONLY with a valid JSON object containing maturity_score, opportunities, next_steps, and key_weaknesses.

answers.companyDescription: Precision metal fabrication shop specializing in CNC-machined aluminum and titanium components for aerospace and automotive Tier-1 suppliers. We run 12 CNC machining centers across two shifts, focusing on high-precision geometries like turbine blades and complex structural brackets. Currently implementing ISO 9001:2025 certification and evaluating robotic tending automation to increase throughput. A tight-knit operation where everyone wears multiple hats.
answers.pastInitiatives: We installed IoT sensors on 40% of our production equipment to monitor utilization and predict failures. The pilot showed a 15% reduction in unplanned downtime on instrumented machines. We now have a business case approved for full fleet rollout, but procurement and integration with our legacy maintenance system are proving more complex than anticipated.
answers.strategicGoals: Our primary objective is to reduce operating expenses by 15% over the next 2 years while maintaining current output levels. We believe there is significant waste in our manual processes and want to identify the highest-ROI automation opportunities across order processing, invoicing, and customer support workflows. We are not looking to grow headcount – we want to do more with our existing team.
answers.additionalContext: The company operates in a highly regulated environment where quality compliance is non-negotiable, requiring strict control over material traceability and documentation.
answers.teamSize: The founder handles all product and technology decisions personally with occasional input from a part-time freelance developer. There is no formal engineering team — technical work is either done by the founder or outsourced to contractors on a project basis. Innovation bandwidth is essentially limited to whatever the founder can personally drive alongside day-to-day operations.

opportunities.title: CNC Job Scheduling Optimization (Lean Process)
opportunities.rationale: Implementing a basic automated scheduling software module focused purely on optimizing machine utilization and minimizing idle time across the 12 centers. This aligns directly with the efficiency priority without requiring massive capital expenditure.

first_actions: Identify free cloud-based scheduling software options (e.g., ERP module add-on)
Pilot integration on one shift/three machines for 3 months
resources_needed: Subscription fees for basic optimization software (estimated $5k)
execution_plan.success_metric: Reduction in average machine idle time by 10% within 6 months.

opportunities.title: Autonomous Quality Inspection Integration (Computer Vision Pilot)
opportunities.rationale: Investigate a low-cost computer vision system to automate the inspection of critical surface defects on aluminum components. This bold step addresses manual quality bottlenecks and could dramatically improve precision consistency, though initial setup requires significant technical skill.

first_actions: Identify 5 critical defect types across top products
Research open-source computer vision libraries (e.g., OpenCV)
Secure a small external developer contract for prototyping
execution_plan.success_metric: Achieving 95% automated defect detection accuracy for specified surface flaws.
milestones: Month 6: Pilot integration on one critical product line
Month 9: Decision to scale or abandon project

next_steps.action: Formalize an Efficiency Task Force charter and establish clear KPIs for the next 18 months
Initiate a detailed cost-benefit analysis for the CNC scheduling optimization project (Opportunity 1)

key_weaknesses: Lack of formal, documented innovation pipeline or structured R&D allocation.
High dependence on the founder's personal technical expertise and bottleneck risk during growth.
Fragmented process management across order processing, production, and customer support workflows.
Strict budget constraint (4%) limits capacity for necessary capital expenditure required for true digital maturity.
